ball.q: Renton were banned in 1890 for a friendly against Edinburgh Saints. Who were Edinburgh Saints really?
ball.a: St Bernard's, a club already suspended for paying players, in disguise

ball.q: On his Celtic debut at Hibs in 1997, Henrik Larsson came off the bench and made a pass. What happened?
ball.a: He gave it straight to Hibs' Chic Charnley, who scored, and Celtic lost 2-1

ball.q: A teenager stabbed Partick Thistle's Chic Charnley with a samurai sword during training in a Glasgow park. What did Charnley do?
ball.a: Disabled him with a punch, despite a stab wound to his hand
ball.sub: Charnley was sent off 17 times in his career.

ball.q: Referee Dougie Smith dropped his yellow card at Ibrox in 1995. Paul Gascoigne picked it up and jokingly booked him. What did Smith do?
ball.a: Booked Gascoigne
ball.sub: It was against Hibernian, on 30 December 1995.

ball.q: After reports that Rangers keeper Andy Goram had a mild form of schizophrenia, what did fans famously sing?
ball.a: There's only two Andy Gorams
ball.sub: It became the title of a 2002 book of football chants.

ball.q: Rangers fans nicknamed Georgian striker Shota Arveladze after which comedy character?
ball.a: Mr Bean
ball.sub: For his likeness to Rowan Atkinson.

ball.q: A Finnish composer wrote a symphonic poem about Rangers striker Duncan Ferguson's jail term. Which Glasgow prison is it named after?
ball.a: Barlinnie, the piece is Barlinnie Nine

ball.q: The Irish striker who scored 44 league goals for Rangers in 1931-32 had which rather ironic surname?
ball.a: English, he was Sam English

ball.q: A Celtic fan tapped Milan keeper Dida on the shoulder during a 2007 Champions League game. What did Dida do?
ball.a: Chased him, then collapsed clutching his face and was stretchered off
ball.sub: UEFA banned him for feigning injury.

ball.q: At half-time of Celtic's Scottish Cup defeat to Inverness in 2000, what did Mark Viduka reportedly do?
ball.a: Threw his boots in the bin and refused to play the second half

ball.q: Roy Keane's first game for Celtic, in January 2006, was a Scottish Cup tie against a second-tier club. What happened?
ball.a: Celtic lost 2-1 to Clyde

ball.q: What happened to Graeme Souness in his first league game as Rangers player-manager, at Hibs in 1986?
ball.a: He was sent off, for two yellow cards inside 34 minutes

ball.q: Homesick and with no English, young Celtic signing Stiliyan Petrov learned the language by working where?
ball.a: In a friend's burger van

ball.q: Alex Ferguson was blamed for a Billy McNeill goal in the 1969 Scottish Cup final. What did Rangers do with him?
ball.a: Dropped him to play for the junior side

ball.q: Richard Gough captained Rangers through nine in a row. In which European capital was he born?
ball.a: Stockholm
ball.sub: His mother was Swedish, and he grew up in South Africa.

ball.q: Celtic signed Mark Viduka in December 1998. What did he do that same month, before playing a game?
ball.a: He quit the club, citing stress
ball.sub: He came back and was the players' player of the year a season later.

ball.q: Celtic's registration of Jorge Cadete was held up for weeks in 1996. What happened to the Scottish FA chief behind it?
ball.a: Jim Farry was found to have delayed it on purpose and lost his job

ball.q: How many goals did Joe Baker score for Hibs in a single Scottish Cup tie against Peebles Rovers?
ball.a: Nine

ball.q: Ally McCoist played a striker in a football film released in 2002. Which Hollywood star led the cast?
ball.a: Robert Duvall, in A Shot at Glory

ball.q: Celtic released a 15-year-old Andy Robertson from their youth set-up in 2009. What was the reported reason?
ball.a: He was too small

ball.q: In December 1995 the referee dropped his yellow card. Paul Gascoigne picked it up and showed it to him. What happened next?
ball.a: The referee, Dougie Smith, booked Gascoigne
ball.sub: It was Rangers against Hibernian.

ball.q: Pierre van Hooijdonk turned down a rise of about 7,000 pounds a week from Celtic. Who did he say it was good enough for?
ball.a: The homeless
ball.sub: He moved to Nottingham Forest instead.

ball.q: Henrik Larsson came off the bench on his Celtic debut at Hibs in 1997. Where did his first pass go?
ball.a: Straight to Hibs' Chic Charnley, who scored the winner
ball.sub: Celtic lost 2-1.

ball.q: Dundee United kept missing penalties in their 1976 relegation fight. Who volunteered to take them?
ball.a: Their goalkeeper, Hamish McAlpine
ball.sub: He scored against Hibs, missed at Ibrox on the last day, and United still stayed up.

ball.q: In 2004 Nicolas Anelka's brother Claude put about 300,000 pounds into Raith Rovers. What did he get for it?
ball.a: The manager's job
ball.sub: He managed one draw and seven defeats in his eight games.

ball.q: Rangers paid 2.2 million pounds for Daniel Prodan in 1998. How many competitive games did he play for them?
ball.a: None, he had a bad knee injury and no medical was done
ball.sub: Rangers released him in January 2001.

ball.q: Before Aberdeen cleared the Pittodrie site for football in 1899, what was it?
ball.a: A dung hill for police horses

ball.q: Motherwell's Fir Park main stand stops about 20 yards short of the end of the pitch. Why?
ball.a: A local resident objected that it would block the light to their garden

ball.q: Kilmarnock fans adopted Paper Roses as their anthem. Which singer surprised them by performing it at Rugby Park in 2013?
ball.a: Marie Osmond

ball.q: Before the 1971 League Cup final, the BBC's Sam Leitch said Partick Thistle had what chance against Celtic?
ball.a: No chance. Thistle won 4-1, and led 4-0 at half-time.

ball.q: Hibs sacked George Best in 1980 after a heavy drinking session. Who was he drinking with?
ball.a: The French rugby team, in Edinburgh to play Scotland
ball.sub: Hibs took him back about a week later.

ball.q: Hamilton Accies were docked 15 points and relegated in 2000 because they failed to play a match. Why?
ball.a: Their unpaid players went on strike

ball.q: Which Dundee director of 2003, known as the Devil's Advocate, later claimed to be on Saddam Hussein's legal team?
ball.a: Giovanni di Stefano
ball.sub: The SFA refused to confirm him because of his fraud convictions.

ball.q: Airdrieonians' last ever match, away at Ayr in April 2002, was abandoned. Why?
ball.a: Protesting Airdrie fans invaded the pitch and broke a crossbar
ball.sub: The club ceased trading days later.

ball.q: Craig Whyte bought Rangers for one pound in 2011. How much did he sell his stake for a year later?
ball.a: Two pounds
ball.sub: Rangers had gone into administration in between.

ball.q: Rangers and Real Zaragoza finished level in the 1966-67 Cup Winners' Cup. How did Rangers go through?
ball.a: On the toss of a coin

ball.q: Chris Woods' British record run without conceding ended at Ibrox in January 1987. What else did that goal do?
ball.a: Knocked Rangers out of the Scottish Cup, Hamilton won 1-0
ball.sub: Adrian Sprott scored it in the 70th minute.

ball.q: Celtic boss Tommy Burns said in 1996 that if anyone did his tombstone it would have to read what?
ball.a: Andy Goram broke my heart

ball.q: John Hartson kicked Eyal Berkovic in the head in West Ham training. What did Berkovic say about it?
ball.a: If my head had been a ball, it would have been in the top corner

ball.q: What did Paul Gascoigne reportedly leave in the sock of young Rangers signing Gennaro Gattuso in 1997?
ball.a: His own poo, he defecated in it

ball.q: Gil Heron was Celtic's first black player, in 1951. His son became famous in America as what?
ball.a: A poet and musician, Gil Scott-Heron
ball.sub: They did not meet again until Scott-Heron was 26.

ball.q: How did Celtic's Patsy Gallacher score against Dundee in the 1925 Scottish Cup final?
ball.a: He somersaulted over the line with the ball wedged between his feet

ball.q: Rangers defender Marvin Andrews hurt his cruciate ligament in 2004-05. Why did he carry on playing instead of resting?
ball.a: He believed God would keep him fit

ball.q: Rangers paid Atlético Madrid 2.2 million pounds for Romanian defender Daniel Prodan in 1998. How many first team games did he play?
ball.a: None. A knee injury kept him out for two and a half years.

ball.q: Hibernian sacked which Manchester United legend in 1980 after a drinking session with the French rugby team?
ball.a: George Best
ball.sub: He was paid per game, and was back in the side a week later.

ball.q: Which blond Argentina World Cup star signed for Dundee in 2000?
ball.a: Claudio Caniggia

ball.q: Rangers signed this French defender on a free from Auxerre in 2004 and sold him to Newcastle for 8 million pounds six months later. Who?
ball.a: Jean-Alain Boumsong

ball.q: Hibernian sacked Russell Latapy in 2001 after a night out that broke their 48 hour drinking rule. Which famous striker was he out with?
ball.a: Dwight Yorke

ball.q: Sunderland made him Britain's most expensive keeper in 2007. Celtic signed him in 2014 after two years without a club. Who?
ball.a: Craig Gordon
ball.sub: Sunderland had paid Hearts 9 million pounds. Knee injuries then kept him out for two years.

ball.q: Henrik Larsson cost Celtic a fee in 1997 that now looks absurd. Roughly how much did they pay Feyenoord?
ball.a: 650,000 pounds

ball.q: Which striker, who scored five goals in one game at the 1994 World Cup, signed for Rangers the following year?
ball.a: Oleg Salenko
ball.sub: He came from Valencia and lasted one season.

ball.q: Steven Naismith's move from Kilmarnock to Rangers in 2007 went through very close to the deadline. How close?
ball.a: 19 seconds before the transfer window shut
